newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan January index of leading indicators rise.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan January index of leading indicators rise.

text.p: Taiwan's index of leading business indicators, which forecasts peaks and troughs in the business cycle, rose for the fifth consecutive month in December, the cabinet said on Tuesday.
The index climbed 1.2 percent to 102.5 in January from December, marking the highest level since June of 1995, the cabinet's Council for Economic Planning and Development said in a statement.
But the index of coincident indicators fell slightly in January, losing 0.3 percent to 101.5 from a month ago.
The council said the economy remained in a "green light" condition, indicating a possible recovery, for the third straight month.
"This shows that the status of the economy is in a stable recovery," the council said.

A relatively high economic growth of 6.62 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996, which took many economists by surprise, has made both the government and private investors sanguine about Taiwan's economic prospect for 1997 -- and helped trigger a sizzling rally in the stock market.
Eighteen percent of a sample polling of manufacturing executives said the economy would improve, the same percentage as the one yielded in a January survey, the agency said.
The percentage of executives who said the economy would grow worse dropped to 17 percent from 21 percent in January.
The rest said the economy would remain unchanged.
